title: Tale of Ali bin Bakkar and Shams al-Nahar

full_text:
In the golden reign of Harun al-Rashid, Prince Ali bin Bakkar, descendant of ancient Persian kings, resided in Baghdad. He was celebrated across the city for his supreme elegance, generosity, and mastery of poetry. One afternoon, visiting the grand jewelers’ souk of Abu al-Hasan, he beheld Shams al-Nahar, the favorite lady of the court, whose countenance shone like the morning sun.

A deep and mutual affection sprang between them, founded on shared reverence for music, poetry, and noble character. Knowing the perilous boundaries of courtly protocol, they met only in secret garden pavilions, exchanging verses of sublime beauty while the lutes played in the moonlight.

Yet the shadow of discovery hung heavy over their heads. When rumors reached the palace, court guards surrounded the pavilion. With swift presence of mind, Abu al-Hasan helped the young prince escape across the river, while Shams al-Nahar returned with composure to the palace, shielding her beloved from royal wrath.

Separated by impassable walls and weighed down by sorrow, Ali bin Bakkar fell into a burning fever in his Baghdad residence, attended by his devoted companions. Shams al-Nahar, confined to the palace, poured her heart into letters of unmatched eloquence, affirming that true love seeks not selfish triumph, but the spiritual elevation and honor of the beloved.

When the Caliph Harun al-Rashid finally discovered their secret correspondence, he was so moved by the chaste purity and poetic nobility of their devotion that his wrath melted into profound compassion. Though fate decreed their earthly parting, their memory was preserved in the songs of Baghdad as an enduring testament to love that transcends all worldly pride.
moral: True devotion endures with dignity through severe trials, finding purity of soul beyond worldly obstacles.
